text:
alex (devex): Quick find — onboarding sampleapp produced duplicate charges when the auth token rotated during submit. Repro below, looking for concise SDK recommendations we can include in the quickstart.

mira (sdk): short question: where do you persist the pending request and what do you replay?

alex (devex): localStorage with full body + idempotencyKey. On reload we just re-POST the stored payload. Code snippet: `localStorage.setItem('pending', JSON.stringify(req))` then on mount `if (pending) fetch(pending.endpoint, {body: pending.body})`.

sam (platform): storing the full body + blind replay is the root cause. If the original finishes after a token refresh and the client replays, server may create duplicate resources.

mira (sdk): recommended short checklist for docs: 1) persist only minimal metadata (idempotencyKey, endpoint, createdAt); 2) do an idempotency lookup (HEAD/GET) on resume; 3) treat 202 as in-flight and poll status instead of re-POSTing; 4) subscribe to auth events and defer automatic replays while refresh is in-flight; 5) never persist secrets/PII.

alex (devex): Can the JS SDK ship a helper for (2)+(4)? That would keep sampleapps consistent.

mira (sdk): yes, we can add `sdk.idempotency.resumeSafely(pending)` implementing: checkIdempotency -> if complete return payload -> if in_progress poll -> if missing create new attempt with a new key and mark old key retired client-side. It will also listen for `auth:refresh` to pause immediate replays.

sam (platform): also recommend server-side: accept idempotency keys with a client namespace and make dedupe window explicit in API docs. That reduces cross-client collisions.

ci-bot: CI: sampleapps/onboarding #204 passed :white_check_mark:

alex (devex): great, I'll update the sampleapp to stop persisting bodies, wire the new helper, and add an e2e that simulates token rotation to prevent regressions. I'll tag the PR with "sdk-idempotency". Thanks!
